Case study · iOS game · Swift Student Challenge 2026

Path of Stillness: a narrative iOS game

I designed and built Path of Stillness solo in 3 days for Apple’s Swift Student Challenge 2026: a four-chapter samurai game where the mechanics themselves teach discipline, without a single control instruction.

Role
Concept, game and interaction design, code, art direction
Team
Solo
Timeline
3 days
Tools
Swift, SwiftUI, SpriteKit, Figma, Gemini (pixel assets)

The problem

The Swift Student Challenge asks for an app built in Swift that solves a problem or offers a unique interaction on Apple devices. I wanted to make values like discipline and self-mastery land for young adults like me, in a way that’s felt rather than lectured.

Why it matters

Discipline is something I practise myself: a year of running every week without a skip, and daily habits for body and mind. Most “self-improvement” content tells you what to do. A game can make you do it, and discover the meaning yourself.

Process

  1. Two days of thinking before building. I researched and planned the full concept before writing code, so the 3 days of execution had a clear vision.
  2. Mood and world. Moodboards for a calm, retro samurai world: wooden dojo, paper screens, pixel art.
  3. Mechanics as meaning. Each chapter shows only one line about a value. The player has to work out the action from that line. No controls are ever explained.
  4. Fitting the constraints. The challenge limits playtime to about 3 minutes and app size to a few MB. Pixel art kept the build under 2 MB; I cut extra animation poses, not story.
  5. Art direction with AI. With no time to draw every sprite, I art-directed the pixel assets with Gemini and assembled them myself.

The four chapters

ChapterValueWhat the player discovers
I · The Weight of StillnessPatienceHolding the screen steady for 10 seconds is what draws the sword
II · The Unbroken RhythmConsistencyThe training post only falls to repeated swipes, again and again
III · The Price of GoldIntegrityChoosing gold over your values sends you back to replay the chapter
IV · The Shadow WithinSelf-masteryAttacking the shadow makes it stronger; you win by not fighting, because the shadow is you

Result

A complete, playable four-chapter game, under 2 MB, finishing within the challenge’s time limit, submitted to Swift Student Challenge 2026.

Impact

It didn’t win. 20+ players from my cohort and the iOS program played it. Most enjoyed it and understood the meaning; a few found the hint-only design confusing at first, then said it clicked once they understood the idea.

Conclusion

The lesson: interaction itself can carry a message. Removing instructions made players think, which is the whole point of a game about stillness. With more time, I’d add small layers of meaning, not more length.
